AMPM Management – Final App Decision Brief & Developer Requirements (PDF, 14 pages, 25 Oct 2026)

Q1.decision: Native iOS and Android apps are required. Offline access to essential wedding-day information is required, with automatic synchronisation when the device reconnects, conflict detection and a controlled resolution process. The final technical architecture is to be agreed with the development team. Decided 26 October 2026: the client portals (hotel discovery and the wedding portal) also run in the browser, and both apps support iPad and Android tablets as well as phones.

Q2.decision: AMPM creates the client's account or sends an invitation link. The client enters basic wedding details (couple's names, contact information, tentative dates, preferred locations) and pays the subscription online by card or UPI. The gateway provider will be selected by AMPM. Payments must create a record, activate the subscription once, and be reviewable by authorised staff. Decided 26 October 2026: Razorpay is the gateway.

Q3.decision: The subscription is for hotel discovery only: Rs 50,000, one-time, one month from activation, configurable in settings. Renewal is a new purchase. After expiry the client keeps read-only access to saved hotel names and existing enquiries; nothing is deleted; renewal restores access and data. There is no separate trial: the demo, reached by mobile OTP, serves that purpose. Decided 26 October 2026: the demo has no time limit, shows three locations with one real hotel each at indicative prices, and is managed by the admin; no refund is offered on the subscription.

Q4.decision: Hotel discovery is a separate paid service. The wedding management fee is decided separately by AMPM, outside the app, and never derived from the subscription. Internal costs, margins, vendor rates, quotations, commissions and negotiations are never shown to clients. Vendor profiles and service details are visible only after AMPM is appointed. Online collection of wedding milestone payments is not required in the first release unless AMPM separately approves it.
open: Which client-facing amounts appear in the wedding portal (budget summary, approved amounts, invoices, payment status)
Which hotel-assistance services beyond availability checks carry a fee

Q5.decision: Only two nominated family representatives use the client portal, one from the bride's side and one from the groom's side; the families decide who. No other family member may hold an account without AMPM's authorisation. Cost and margin information is never visible to them. AMPM may record a decision made outside the portal when a note or supporting record is attached. Confirmed 26 October 2026: the client-portal access and permission rules of the brief's section 5 stand as written. Working decision on logins: two individually authenticated accounts, the brief's stated preference, to be countersigned.
open: Login implementation: working decision of 26 October 2026 is two individually authenticated accounts; AMPM to countersign
Whether one representative's approval completes a decision or both must approve

Q6.decision: AMPM manages the system and controls permissions. Staff access is restricted by assigned responsibilities and department; a department manager on a phone sees only their own sections. Functional departments named: hotel team, vendor team, RSVP team, hospitality team, production team, project manager, senior authorised management. Internal financial information is restricted to specifically authorised personnel.
open: Final staff role list and which users may see hotel costs and vendor costs

Q7.decision: Guest invitation links are issued per side (one for the bride's side, one for the groom's side) or as one combined link when AMPM chooses; the final structure is to be decided. The RSVP team imports or creates the guest list and sends the links. Guests cannot see other households or the guest list, and cannot edit a submitted response; corrections go through a change request or the help option to the RSVP caller. The two family representatives see approved RSVP summaries and cannot edit the list. Each guest is counted individually, children included; meal preference, allergies where required, rooming and travel where applicable are collected.
open: Final link structure: per side, or one combined link

Q8.decision: Identity documents may be collected only where a hotel requires them for a wedding, under AMPM's control, in restricted storage, visible only to authorised staff, and never Aadhaar documents or numbers. Nothing is deleted automatically; retention and deletion follow AMPM-approved policy, to be confirmed before launch.
open: Retention period and privacy wording for identity documents

Q9.decision: Eva maintains the existing hotel data and updates seasonal prices roughly three times a year. Hotel pages show hotel and venue details, rooms, photographs and videos, food and menu information in a grid, approximate room pricing, wedding package price ranges, indicative venue rental, approximate per-plate pricing, capacity and facilities, and street view or map location. Prices are indicative ranges with a last-verified date, never internal cost. Availability is checked by the team when a client requests it or adds a hotel to their selection. Previous clients' photographs appear only with permission, controlled by AMPM. Hotels can be imported from spreadsheets. About 200 hotels at the start.

Q10.decision: The first release includes the demo and the subscription hotel-discovery workflow, wedding management after appointment, vendor selection, the client portal, department-based team access, RSVP, tracked requests, live chat and offline wedding-day operations. It excludes website editing, online milestone payments and GST invoicing. Only Eva's authorised personnel may approve operational exceptions; the authority must be configurable. Decided 26 October 2026: the whole first release goes live at once, in one launch.

Q11.decision: Email and WhatsApp are required; SMS is proposed. Live chat is also required on the home page. Providers are to be confirmed.

Q12.decision: No. AMPM staff will not edit public website content through the app in the initial scope; the website editor is not approved.

Q13.decision: Prospects, demo users and clients sign in with their mobile number and an OTP. There is no unrestricted self-registration; AMPM creates the account or sends an invitation. Staff have individual authorised accounts with role- and department-based access; the exact staff authentication method is to be finalised with the development team. Decided 26 October 2026: a client is verified by both email and mobile number; sign-in stays by mobile number and OTP. Decided 26 October 2026: staff sign in with a password and an authenticator-app code; the identity service is Amazon Cognito in Mumbai.

Q14.decision: Hosting arrangements, backup frequency and recovery timelines are yet to be confirmed with the developer. Decided 26 October 2026: everything runs on AMPM's dedicated VPS, a Hostinger KVM 4 in the India (Mumbai) datacentre, with pgBackRest archives to a Mumbai S3 bucket and rehearsed monthly restores (recovery point about one minute, rebuild within four hours), files and identity documents in Mumbai buckets, Cognito for identity; the specification is docs/engineering/vps-setup.md.

Q15.decision: About 200 hotels at the start and roughly 20 concurrent weddings as a planning assumption; multiple weddings and departmental staff access; staff and guest capacity to be confirmed.
open: Staff count and largest guest count

Q16.decision: Indian rupees. English as the primary language. The platform will not issue GST invoices.

Q17.decision: AMPM will decide the final privacy wording and the data retention policy. Retention and deletion require AMPM's approval; guest and wedding information must remain access-controlled; wedding records are not deleted automatically.
open: Retention periods for leads, guest records and identity documents

Q18.decision: Yes. A wedding can involve multiple hotels and venues.

Q19.decision: Room blocks by hotel, room category and dates. Allocation and rooming are handled by the team, not automatically. Counts must support both room-wise and person-wise calculations, children included.

Q20.decision: Both tracked requests with conversation history and live chat are required; live chat on the home page, distinguished from tracked requests so a formal change request keeps its own approval history. More options may be added later.

Q21.decision: Change requests are submitted, reviewed, accepted or rejected, then implemented and closed. A change to an approved item creates a new version for approval.

Q22.decision: No vendor or hotel logins in the current version.

Q23.decision: Read-only client access for three months after the wedding, then the project is archived following AMPM's approval. Records are not deleted; archiving is a change of status and permissions. Later access or reopening is controlled by AMPM.
open: Exact workflow for archiving and for restoring access after archiving

Q24.decision: A short feedback form after the wedding and an archived state that preserves the records.

Q25.decision: Thresholds must be configurable; AMPM will define the final budget-change percentages, date-change and venue-change thresholds and the approval rules.

additional_requirements: Demo: reached after mobile OTP verification; up to three locations with street view where available; one or two sample hotels per location with indicative prices (to be finalised); limited hotel information; duration to be finalised; the client may request a 15 to 20 minute Zoom call before purchasing.
Account activation: the client completes basic wedding details (couple's names, contact information, tentative dates, preferred locations) before paying.

Hotel page content: food and menu information in a grid, vegetarian and non-vegetarian menus, approximate per-plate pricing, wedding package price ranges, indicative venue rental, approximate room pricing, street view or map; the portal must distinguish indicative, requested, verified and awaiting-confirmation information.
Selection or cart: adding a hotel to the selection can trigger an availability request to the hotel team.

Vendor categories include photography and videography, decor and production, catering, entertainment and artists, makeup and styling, transport and logistics, and others per AMPM's service structure. Vendor contact details stay internal by default; AMPM may share specific contacts in an approved case.
Tracked request statuses: submitted, under review, accepted, rejected, implemented, closed.

Offline scope for staff: assigned tasks, department information, readiness checklists, cue sheets, arrival and operational lists; offline updates where supported; the app shows offline state and pending sync, never silently loses updates, detects conflicts with a controlled resolution, and protects locally stored data; offline data limited to the user's role.
Readiness exceptions record the unmet check, the exception and reason, the authorised person, the time and the resulting status; only Eva's authorised personnel may approve them.
Configurable settings: subscription price and duration, demo limits, hotel categories, vendor categories, pricing thresholds, change-request rules, access and approval settings.
Public website: company information, enquiry submission, demo requests, contact details, login and invitation entry points; no editing by staff.
The platform is for AMPM's internal business use, not for licensing to other wedding planners.
Both apps, the team app and the client app, on iOS and Android, must support iPad and Android tablets as well as phones (26 October 2026).
A client is verified by both email and mobile number; sign-in is by mobile number and OTP (26 October 2026).
The demo is managed by the admin: no time limit, three locations, one real hotel per location with indicative prices (26 October 2026).
